accepted.title: Three upward families: singleton-cell product bound
accepted.text: Let A, B, C be upward-closed subsets of the Boolean lattice 2^[n], each of the same uniform density α. Put a=μ(A∩Bᶜ∩Cᶜ), b=μ(Aᶜ∩B∩Cᶜ), and c=μ(Aᶜ∩Bᶜ∩C), where μ is uniform probability. Is ab+ac+bc≤16/243 for every n and every such triple?
accepted.citation: Conjecture 1.1.8, printed p. 3 / PDF p. 11; definitions §1.1, PDF pp. 9–11.

accepted.title: Minimum cube dimension for non-layered graphs of large girth
accepted.text: For even g≥6, let N(g) be the least n such that the n-dimensional hypercube graph Q_n has a subgraph of girth exactly g that is not isomorphic to a subgraph of any edge layer of any hypercube. An edge layer consists of vertices of Hamming weights k−1 and k with all cube edges between them. Determine the asymptotic growth of N(g) as g→∞ through even integers.

accepted.title: Almost maximum independent sets of toroidal queens
accepted.text: For each fixed integer d≥3, does there exist C_d such that, for all sufficiently large positive integers n, at least n^(d−1)−C_d n^(d−2) pairwise nonattacking queens can be placed on (ℤ/nℤ)^d? Distinct positions attack exactly when their difference equals λe for a nonzero e∈{−1,0,1}^d and a nonzero λ∈ℤ/nℤ. There is no restriction on the prime factors of n.
accepted.citation: Conjecture 6.2.3, printed p. 49 / PDF p. 57; queen definition §6.1 and proof of Theorem 6.2.2. Later paper: Conjecture 2, arXiv:2404.18237v3.

accepted.title: Greedy conference gossiping below full dissemination
accepted.text: Initially each of n people knows a distinct gossip item. In a conference call exactly k people all learn the union of the items they currently know. The score is the sum, over people, of the number of items known. For fixed integers 3≤k≤n and 0≤m below the minimum number of k-person calls required for everyone to know all n items, does every greedy m-call sequence attain the largest possible final score? A greedy sequence chooses at each step a call maximizing the immediate score increase, with arbitrary choices among ties.
accepted.citation: Question 7.3.1, printed p. 61 / PDF p. 69; September 22, 2026 journal version, Conjecture 3.2.
accepted.subject: Combinatorics & Graph Theory
accepted.literature_finding: The September 2026 publication still states the conference-call extension as conjectural. Pairwise calls and the forest range m(k−1)≤n−1 are proved. The question here retains the full conference-call ambition; no resolution of the remaining range located.

accepted.title: Everywhere Borel matching from a connected toast
accepted.text: Does every d-regular bipartite Borel graph, for finite d≥1, that admits a connected toast have a Borel perfect matching on its entire vertex set? A connected toast is a Borel family T of finite vertex sets with ∪_{K∈T}E(K)=E(G); for distinct K,L∈T, either B₁(K)∩L=∅, B₁(K)⊆L, or B₁(L)⊆K; and each induced graph on K minus the union of the proper T-subsets of K is connected. Here B₁(K) is the closed graph neighborhood (Definition 3.2.2).
accepted.citation: Question 3.1.6, printed p. 19 / PDF p. 26; Definition 3.2.2, §3.2. Paper counterpart: Question 2 in arXiv:2210.14300.
accepted.subject: Logic & Foundations
accepted.literature_finding: The thesis and published-author text retain the everywhere question. Measurable/generic matching results and the newer measurable spanning-tree theorem do not give an everywhere Borel perfect matching. No exact closure found.

accepted.title: Treeability of Archimedean orders on ℤ³
accepted.text: Is the orbit equivalence relation E(GL₃(ℤ) acting on Ar(ℤ³)) treeable? Ar(A) is the standard Borel space of Archimedean translation-invariant total orders on the additive group A; GL₃(ℤ) acts on Ar(ℤ³) by transporting orders. Treeable means generated by a Borel acyclic graph.

accepted.title: Borel complexity of Archimedean orders over ℤ[1/n]
accepted.text: For integers n≥2, determine the Borel complexity of the isomorphism relation of Archimedean orders on the additive group ℤ[1/n]², equivalently the orbit equivalence relation of GL₂(ℤ[1/n]) acting on Ar(ℤ[1/n]²). Here ℤ[1/n]={a/n^j:a∈ℤ,j≥0}, and orders are identified when a group automorphism transports one to the other.

accepted.title: Borel reducibility between ranks of Archimedean orders
accepted.text: Let E_r be the orbit equivalence relation of GL_r(ℤ) on Ar(ℤ^r), the space of Archimedean orders on the additive group ℤ^r. Determine the Borel reducibility relations between these ranks: for sufficiently large integers n<m, can E_m≤_B E_n hold, and does E_n≤_B E_m always hold? A Borel reduction f must satisfy x E y if and only if f(x) F f(y).

accepted.literature_finding: The source retains both directions as questions. Hyperfiniteness and treeability results alone do not settle the full reducibility pattern. No later answer located.

accepted.title: Amenability of ideal Bernoulli Voronoi tessellations
accepted.text: Fix a countable nonamenable group Γ, a left-invariant proper metric, and a fixed measurable equivariant rule assigning nearest-center ties. Independently retain each group element as a center with probability p and partition Γ into its Voronoi cells. An ideal Bernoulli Voronoi tessellation is any subsequential weak limit, as p↓0, of the resulting invariant random equivalence relations. Must every such limit be amenable as an invariant random equivalence relation (in the source’s Definition 3.7 sense)? The unresolved target includes nonexact groups; exact groups have an affirmative answer.
accepted.citation: Question 6.6.2, printed p. 120 / PDF p. 127; construction §6.6, PDF pp. 126–127. March 27, 2026 accepted paper: §6, Question 1, arXiv:2502.11622v2; amenability Definition 3.7 there.
accepted.subject: Logic & Foundations
accepted.literature_finding: The March 2026 accepted version proves amenability for exact groups, produces nonamenable limits of other finite IREs on nonexact groups, and explicitly leaves this specific Voronoi question open. No later solution found.

accepted.title: Indistinguishability of ideal Bernoulli Voronoi cells
accepted.text: Fix a countable nonamenable group Γ, a left-invariant proper metric, and a fixed measurable equivariant rule assigning nearest-center ties. Independently retain each group element as a center with probability p and partition Γ into its Voronoi cells. An ideal Bernoulli Voronoi tessellation is any subsequential weak limit, as p↓0, of the resulting invariant random equivalence relations. Must every such limit have indistinguishable cells? Indistinguishability means that every measurable Γ-equivariant cell selection rule is almost surely trivial (it selects all cells or no cells).
accepted.citation: First question in Question 6.6.4, printed p. 120 / PDF p. 127; cell-selection definition immediately before it. March 27, 2026 accepted paper: §6, first question in Question 3, arXiv:2502.11622v2.
accepted.subject: Logic & Foundations
accepted.literature_finding: The accepted paper retains this discrete Bernoulli question. The cited indistinguishability theorem concerns ideal Poisson tessellations on symmetric spaces, not all discrete groups. No closure of the exact discrete target found.
accepted.scope_review: Only the first, Voronoi-specific question of source Question 6.6.4 is promoted; the broader second question remains unnumbered.

accepted.title: Does a convex belief-propagation image imply universal fields?
accepted.text: For an interaction matrix A and a distribution μ on [q]^d, set G_c(μ)=E_μ[∏_{i=1}^d A_{c,τ_i}] and F_c(μ)=G_c(μ)/∑_b G_b(μ), wherever the denominator is positive. Let F_prod be the image of product distributions and F_all the image of all distributions under F. For a symmetric entrywise nonnegative interaction matrix A∈ℝ^(q×q) and integer d with F_prod=F_all, do there exist d fixed nonnegative external-field arrays λ^(i)∈ℝ^(d×q), independent of μ, such that F(μ)=F(⊗_{i=1}^d(λ^(i)⋆μ)_i) for every admissible μ? Here λ⋆μ(τ) is proportional to μ(τ)∏_j λ_{j,τ_j}, and (λ⋆μ)_i denotes its i-th marginal. The arrays must make these tilts and F well defined for the distributions to which the identity applies.
accepted.citation: Question 3.9.17, printed p. 163 / PDF p. 163; definitions §3.8.1, Proposition 3.8.3, Definition 3.9.2. Later/current paper: Question 3, arXiv:2411.06541v2.
accepted.subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
accepted.literature_finding: The February 2025 revision retains this conditional universal-fields question. The general reduction is disproved, but that disproof does not establish a counterexample under F_prod=F_all. No later answer located.

accepted.title: Convex image of product measures for antiferromagnetic Potts
accepted.text: Fix integers q≥3 and d≥2 and max{0,1−q/(d+1)}≤β≤1. For the antiferromagnetic Potts matrix A=11ᵀ−(1−β)I_q, is the image of product distributions on [q]^d under belief propagation F a convex subset of the probability simplex? For an interaction matrix A and a distribution μ on [q]^d, set G_c(μ)=E_μ[∏_{i=1}^d A_{c,τ_i}] and F_c(μ)=G_c(μ)/∑_b G_b(μ), wherever the denominator is positive. Let F_prod be the image of product distributions and F_all the image of all distributions under F.

accepted.subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes

accepted.title: Uniformly bounded cycle swaps connecting all 3D box tilings
accepted.text: Does there exist a universal finite integer K such that, for every j×m×n rectangular grid box with positive integer side lengths and jmn even, any two perfect matchings can be connected by swaps on alternating cycles of length at most K? The grid joins nearest neighbors. An alternating-cycle swap exchanges matching and nonmatching edges along that cycle. The source also asks the stronger version using only flips and trits (the specified 4-edge square and 6-edge cube moves).
accepted.citation: Problem 2.9.1, printed p. 195 / PDF p. 195; discussion PDF pp. 195–196. Current joint paper: Problem 9.0.1, arXiv:2304.08468v3.
accepted.subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
accepted.literature_finding: The May 2026 revision retains both box-connectivity questions. HLT23 proves existence of at least one flip or trit, which is weaker than connecting every pair. Nonconnectivity for arbitrary simply connected regions does not settle rectangular boxes. No later box resolution found.

accepted.title: Reducing Archimedean-order isomorphism to a rank-three linear action
accepted.text: For which integer ranks n≥2 does the orbit equivalence relation of GL_n(ℤ) acting on Ar(ℤ^n) Borel reduce to the orbit equivalence relation of GL₃(ℤ) acting by matrix multiplication on ℝ³? Ar(ℤ^n) is the standard Borel space of Archimedean translation-invariant total orders on ℤ^n. A Borel reduction f must satisfy x E y if and only if f(x) F f(y). The target is the action on ℝ³, not on Ar(ℤ³).
accepted.citation: Question 5.3.1, printed p. 97 / PDF p. 104; paper counterpart Question 3.1, arXiv:2403.11326. The literal fixed rank-three target is retained from both sources.
accepted.subject: Logic & Foundations
accepted.literature_finding: The paper and April 2026 thesis retain this comparison question. It differs from the within-family rank comparison because its target is a linear action on vectors rather than transported orders. No later resolution found. The source leaves n as a parameter; the promoted classification question keeps n variable and asks which ranks admit a reduction.

accepted.title: Borel degree of isomorphism across all finitely generated Archimedean orders
accepted.text: Determine the Borel complexity of the equivalence relation E on the disjoint union ⨆_{n≥2} Ar(ℤ^n) that identifies two Archimedean ordered groups exactly when they are isomorphic as ordered groups. Within a rank n, equivalence is the orbit relation of GL_n(ℤ) acting by transport of orders; distinct ranks are inequivalent. The classification target is the Borel reducibility degree of this countable union, including how it compares to the individual rank relations.
accepted.citation: Question 5.3.3 and displayed disjoint union, printed p. 97 / PDF p. 104; paper counterpart Question 3.3, arXiv:2403.11326.
accepted.subject: Logic & Foundations
accepted.literature_finding: Both current source texts retain the all-ranks complexity question. Higher-rank nonhyperfinite/nontreeable results give lower bounds, not a classification of the Borel degree of the union. No later classification located.

accepted.title: Uniqueness of the low-intensity Bernoulli Voronoi limit
accepted.text: Fix a countable nonamenable group Γ, a left-invariant proper metric, and a fixed measurable equivariant rule assigning nearest-center ties. Independently retain each group element as a center with probability p and partition Γ into its Voronoi cells. An ideal Bernoulli Voronoi tessellation is any subsequential weak limit, as p↓0, of the resulting invariant random equivalence relations. Determine for which groups and fixed metric/tie-rule choices this weak limit is unique, meaning that all subsequences p_j↓0 with a weak limit yield the same distribution on equivalence relations. The metric and tie rule are held fixed when comparing subsequences.
